evidence: EPHE V Section official address list gives Sylvain Lévi: rue Guy-de-Labrosse, 9.
what_it_supports: Fixes Lévi's institutional contact/address in Lovejoy's exact Paris year.
limit: An institutional address list alone does not prove it was the site of Lovejoy's reading sessions.

evidence: AGORHA identifies 9 rue Guy-de-la-Brosse as Lévi's private address from 1894 to 1935.
what_it_supports: Upgrades the same address from mere contact address to documented private residence.
limit: Modern authority record; use EPHE list as contemporary anchor.

evidence: EPHE 1897-98 address list also gives Lévi at 9 rue Guy-de-Labrosse; 1899-1900 list repeats it.
what_it_supports: Shows residence/contact continuity across mission departure, return, and Lovejoy year.

evidence: EPHE 1900-01 Sanskrit report says 'en dehors de ces deux conférences' Lévi continued Bhagavad-Gītā reading with Stickney.
what_it_supports: Direct proof that Lévi conducted individualized/supplementary text reading beyond regular advertised conferences.
limit: Location not specified; not evidence the Stickney work occurred at Lévi's home.

evidence: Mauss later recalled individualized Sanskrit/Indian training with Lévi and Finot, including Pāli/Buddhist translation and a Brāhmaṇa course directed personally to him.
what_it_supports: Shows student-specific instruction was characteristic of Lévi's pedagogy before the mission.
limit: Retrospective; exact Pāli academic year not primary-fixed.

evidence: Lardinois reconstructs that after moving to 9 rue Guy-de-la-Brosse in 1894, the Lévi household developed a regular scholarly salon around the turn of the century, gathering colleagues, students and visitors.
what_it_supports: Makes a home-based scholarly/student setting historically legible at the same residence.
limit: Do not project the later regular weekly salon mechanically onto autumn 1898 or identify Lovejoy as a salon participant.

evidence: Wilson, using Lovejoy letters of 17 Oct, 1 Dec, 5 Dec 1898, says the unavailable Pāli-Buddhism course led Lovejoy occasionally to Lévi's home to read sacred texts with him.
what_it_supports: Direct biographical claim under test; now spatially and pedagogically corroborated by independent controls.
limit: Exact letter wording, texts, language, dates and address remain unrecovered; no direct transcript yet.

evidence: The combined evidence supports a three-layer claim: verified private residence + verified supplementary-text pedagogy + Wilson-mediated Lovejoy home-reading report.
what_it_supports: Raises plausibility and historical specificity of the private-reading episode without converting it into direct manuscript proof.
limit: Triangulation is not replacement for JHU MS-0873.
